lens: design concept, art direction, hierarchy and restraint against ref-02

measurements.units: css px at 816x1056; 1 px = 0.2646 mm; U = 13 px = 3.44 mm
measurements.note: layout.json has no scorecard-format elements[] array. It gives per-preview wordmark, columns, heads, sub heads and eye_travel, so the item-row spacing below was measured from preview-letter.png baselines (display px x1.65 / 3.125).

margins_mm.verdict: pass: all four equal within 0.1 mm. The sun bleeds off the top and right, and the field bleeds 39 px (10.3 mm) past the right trim, so the bleed check passes.

left_edges.verdict: pass: 0.0 deviation for names, heads and sub heads

headers.cross_column_registration: Cocktails and Cider both at y 200, Beer and Wine both at y 707

price_pair_scan.verdict: pass: all prices inline, gap 1.9% of width. The phone figure spans name start to price end; the actual gap is 3.9%.

item_spacing.beer_name_to_name: Czech Pilsner to Dry-Hopped IPA = 7U (91 px); IPA to Amber Lager = 6U (78 px); both have one-line descriptions
item_spacing.cocktails: Margarita to Manhattan = 8U (104 px), with 2- and 1-line descriptions
item_spacing.desc_end_to_next_name: Margarita 70 px, Czech 69 px, IPA 57 px, Manhattan to sub head 58 px
item_spacing.verdict: FAIL: gaps differ by 13 px (3.4 mm), more than 7x the ±0.5 mm tolerance. The balancing search puts spare grid units wherever the heads fall on the field rhythm.

dead_space.verdict: flag: 14 items stretched down the full height with 6-8U row pitch. The gaps between Cocktails and Beer and between Margarita and Manhattan are padding, not grouping. Rows read as floating, not as a list.

contrast_worst_pixel.verdict: pass: the field never sits under text

visual_tests.note: The 10.3 ratio counts only the densest hook band. Perceptually the field strip is the largest high-contrast area on the page (about 32% of the width, full height) and competes with the wordmark.

measurements.horizon: Not level. It rises from about y 408 to 383 in the display preview from left to right, so the sun's clip reads as a drafting error rather than a horizon.

remove: The stepped stair offsets on the hooks (the three-position inward reset). They turn the field into a jittering maze or radiator coil. Keep one nested greca hook shape repeated at a constant x so the step-fret reads as one fret, not as noise.
top_problem: The furrow-field thesis is not visible. The furrows stop at x 552 and never pass under or through the list, so 'every row sits on a furrow' is invisible to the guest. The strip reads as a generic op-art maze beside a ref-02 panel-2 sun, and it fails the substitution test. The missing bold idea: make the plough line actually carry the menu. The furrows run under the columns as the row lines (faint and broken behind the text, full strength only in the margins), and turn in a greca at each section head, so Mexico and Iowa fuse in the reading layer itself.
fixes: Fix the measured spacing failure: use one constant item pitch per section (for example desc-end to next name = 4U everywhere) and put the spare units between sections, not between items, so Beer, Cocktails and Wine rows share one rhythm.

Run the furrow line into the list: one quiet furrow under each item row, broken behind the text and the price, turning in a greca hook at each section head. The thesis then becomes visible structure rather than a side panel.
Cut the field's visual weight: a lighter stroke (about 0.25 mm) or ink-2 instead of ink, and fewer nested returns (2 instead of 3), so the wordmark and sun stay the only dominant region.
Level the horizon to a true horizontal at the sun's clip line. At present the tilt reads as a mistake, not as contour.
Tighten the page to the content: raise the list and reduce the row pitch so the columns read as a grouped list. Give the reclaimed space to a quiet bottom band, not spread across every row gap.

lens: items and prices against build/draft_doc.json; ingredient names and completeness of descriptions (public_components respected); menu flow for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The furrow ornament sets the spacing instead of the content. Margarita to Manhattan leaves a gap of about three rows, which is wider than the break before House Originals. The three beers sit about 170 px apart and a dead hole opens under Cognac VSOP, so items drift away from their sub-heads. The two columns also register row by row (Cocktails beside Cider, Beer beside Wine), which invites reading across the page as well as down. The column order puts Wine last after Spirits, and a one-item Cider section takes the top-right head slot with the same weight as Cocktails.
problems: All 14 items and all 14 prices exactly match the draft: Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13. Nothing is invented and no item is dropped.

The garnishes (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel) are not draft components. They trace to phg.recipe_versions.garnish (recorded in earlier rounds from gateway log 74), so they are sourced. But proposal.md section 9 still calls them unconfirmed, and they should be cited per item in this round's proposal.

public_components is respected: Aromatic Bitters is hidden on the Manhattan. The draft's own public line for the Manhattan ('Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.') contradicts that flag, and Rob needs to settle which one is right.

Known data gap, not the designer's fault: 10 of 14 descriptions only echo the item name ('Blanco tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour', 'Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Dry red wine'). Beer has no ABV or brewery, wine has no region or producer, and spirits have no brand, NOM or age. The printed menu does not flag this as missing_ingredients, so a guest sees a thin list.
The draft's section descriptions ('Classic and house cocktails.', 'Straight pours by category.' and the others) and the subtitle were dropped with no note in proposal.md.

Punctuation is inconsistent. Every description drops its full stop except the Margarita, which reads 'agave syrup · lime wheel. Bright and citrus-forward.' That joins a flavour note onto the garnish in the middle of an ingredient list.

Venue flow: this is an agave-led cantina, but the only two tequilas sit halfway down column 2 under a generic Spirits head. Cider (one item) and Brandy (one item) get the same head and sub-head weight as whole categories.
Prices use one consistent inline style (no $, whole numbers, 15.3 px after the name). This is clean but not distinctive, and the price x-position is ragged by design.
fixes: Space items evenly within each section and put the leftover height between sections, not between items, so each sub-head visibly owns its items and no item floats a triple gap away from its group; let the ornament follow the content spacing, not the other way round.

Reorder to Cocktails, Beer, Cider, Wine, Spirits (with Agave first inside Spirits), or fold the single cider into Beer as 'Beer & Cider', so the reading path runs from lightest to strongest and no single-item category takes the second head slot.

Make description punctuation uniform: either end every line with a full stop, or keep the Margarita's flavour note but separate it from the garnish (for example, the ingredient list, then a new line with 'Bright and citrus-forward').

Replace the name-echo lines for beer, wine and spirits with a visible missing-data flag in the proposal (ABV/brewery, region/producer, brand/NOM/age) and add Rob's data as soon as it lands; do not pad them with invented descriptors.
Record in proposal.md the dropped section descriptions and subtitle, and cite each garnish's recipe_versions id, so that nothing is removed or sourced without a note.

lens: Traced every printed ingredient, garnish and label to build/draft_doc.json and to phg.recipe_versions through phg.menu_items.current_recipe_version_id (gateway log_id 219). Checked how descriptions and prices sit together in explore-H3/preview-letter.png.
top_problem: Every printed fact traces to a source, but the descriptions are not guest copy. Seven of the ten non-cocktail lines only repeat the item name or its category: Blanco Tequila 'Blanco tequila pour', Añejo Tequila 'Añejo tequila pour', Cognac VSOP 'VSOP Cognac pour', Dry Cider 'Dry sparkling cider', Amber Lager 'Toasty amber lager', Dry-Hopped IPA 'Hop-forward draft IPA', Brut Rosé 'Dry sparkling rosé'. 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine' are taxonomy wording. Under criterion 12 that caps the score at 40, and it stays capped even though the missing grape, region, ABV and brand data is a known gap with Rob. Verified sources: Margarita garnish 'Lime wheel' (recipe_versions f06abb74-762a-4f89-81b2-76a9e4714f3c); House Daiquiri 'Lime coin' (recipe_versions 14d45e57-72fa-4d23-8274-24e5c80e4b12); Brown Butter Old Fashioned 'Orange peel' (recipe_versions 7095fd3d-58fb-43f5-8e8f-1a0afadeafa7); Manhattan 'Cocktail cherry' (recipe_versions 9fb77eaa-c5eb-477c-8e21-acbc89a0e942). Aromatic bitters are left off the Manhattan correctly, because draft meta.public_components sets aromatic-bitters to false. All other cocktail ingredients match draft_doc components: Tequila Blanco, Fresh Lime Juice, Orange Liqueur, Agave Syrup, White Rum, Demerara Syrup, Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon, Rye Whiskey, Sweet Vermouth, Aromatic Bitters. All 14 prices match phg.menu_items.menu_price and the draft. Every price sits inline about 15 px after its name, so there is no misassociation. Junmai Ginjo ($12) is in phg.menu_items but not in the draft doc and not printed; the Content reviewer should confirm whether it belongs. Venue fit is weak for a Mexican cantina: agave gets two unlabelled pours buried under Spirits, Cider takes the head of column 2 level with Cocktails, and apart from the wordmark and the item names 'Añejo' and 'Blanco', no section or subhead shows Spanish or cantina voice. The draft title is 'Bar menu'; 'CANTINA' and '& cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa' are venue-type copy, not item facts, so they do not fail the gate. The description voice is split: the Margarita ends with a sentence ('Bright and citrus-forward.') while the other cocktails are bare middot lists. Tequila word order also differs within the menu ('Tequila blanco' in the Margarita against the item 'Blanco Tequila'). Both follow their sources, but the menu reads inconsistently.
fixes: Replace the name-echo descriptions for spirits, beer, cider and wine with a visible missing_ingredients placeholder, or leave the line empty, until Rob supplies grape, region, style, ABV, age and brand. A line that repeats the name adds nothing, and inventing detail is not allowed.

Give agave its cantina weight: rename or kick the Spirits > Agave block in cantina voice (for example 'Agave' promoted to its own section after Cocktails), and move Cider below Wine so the item list and prices do not change. Send this to the designer as a layout note.

Put the description voice on one pattern for all four cocktails. Either every cocktail gets its ingredient list plus a short flavour sentence drawn from its recipe_versions rationale, or the Margarita loses 'Bright and citrus-forward.' so it matches the bare ingredient lists of the other three.

Tighten the item rhythm. In preview-letter.png the gaps between items are uneven: Margarita to Manhattan is about twice the gap of Manhattan to House Originals, and Blanco to Añejo is wider than Añejo to Brandy, so descriptions float as islands. Also fix the House Daiquiri break, which leaves 'lime coin' widowed on its own line.
Label the pour sizes on spirits and the glass pour on wine (for example '1.5 oz' / '5 oz') once Rob confirms them; until then flag them as missing and do not print a guessed size.
